paragraph: The king, all his life, has been famed for his virtue, knowledge and righteousness. If such a man commands me, I will not ask the reason why. I shall only obey and so shall you. It is up to me to help him keep his promise to Kaikeyi. Kshatriya dharma does not permit disobedience to the word of a father, mother or a Brahmin even if they arise out of anger, passion or desire. It is by the order of the king that Kaikeyi banishes me. Perish your thoughts of violence and honour your duty!
Situation/Problem_Faced: Rama is justifying his decision to follow his father’s command and go into exile. He urges Lakshmana to abandon any thoughts of retaliation or resistance and instead embrace duty and non-violence, even in the face of perceived injustice.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama emphasizes obedience to dharma and the importance of upholding promises, even when the situation appears unjust. He refuses to challenge the king’s order or Kaikeyi’s intent, insisting on non-violence and filial duty.
Outcome/Resolution: In this specific interaction, Rama successfully reasserts his unwavering commitment to his father's command and actively dissuades Lakshmana from any rebellious action or thoughts of violence. He establishes the path of duty and non-resistance as the only acceptable course, thereby reinforcing the immediate outcome of his exile.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.stress Management: Composure, Ethical resilience, Calm under pressure
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.relationship Challenges (Family): Conflict of loyalty, Familial tension, Emotional divergence

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dharma (Duty - Rama’s adherence to Kshatriya duty and filial obligation)
Satya (Truth - Fulfilling the father’s promise without deception or deviation)
Ahimsa (Non-violence - Rejecting Lakshmana's idea of retaliation)
Vairagya (Detachment - Rama’s dispassionate acceptance of exile)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Rama embodies 'Dharma' by prioritizing his duty over personal grievances, reflects 'Satya' by upholding his father's promise, and expresses 'Ahimsa' through his call for non-violence. His calm acceptance of exile indicates a deep sense of 'Vairagya'.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Rama models psychological resilience and self-regulation under pressure. He handles emotional conflict and familial discord through calm reasoning and ethical clarity, effectively managing both his own emotions and those of his brother.
